title: Kentucky is already ranked ahead of key rivals, and Mark Pope isn't done adding pieces - NewsBreak
text:
By Lane Mills ,
13 hours ago Nov 21, 2025; Lexington, Kentucky, USA; Kentucky Wildcats head coach Mark Pope talks with his players on the court during the first half against the Loyola (MD) Greyhounds at Rupp Arena at Central Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mark Pope is entering his third year behind the wheel in Lexington with a fair amount of pressure to right the ship. All the same, at this point in the offseason, it's hard for fans to do much else besides pump their jersyes with excitement for the current group. Pope has already put together a solid Kentucky roster, positioning him in front of numerous key rivals.
Per Jon Rothstein's ever-changing preseason top 45, Kentucky comes in all the way up at No. 15. Louisville slots in behind the Wildcats, at No. 16, while Indiana, North Carolina, and Kansas all situate at No. 28, No. 29, and No. 32, respectively. There's an almost objective gap here.
Although, a lot of the Big Blue Nation won't be shy about wanting more from the 15-spot; to that end, Coach Pope is still actively on the recruiting trail for the Cats' final roster spot. Whether or not he'll actually fill it is a question that remains to be seen, but the Wildcats being positioned ahead of four of their five non-conference heavy-hitters, in any ranking, is a noteworthy deal.
Louisville coach Pat Kelsey and Kentucky coach Mark Pope work the sidelines during first half action as the Louisville Cardinals hosted the Kentucky Wildcats at the KFC Yum! Center on Tuesday, Nov. 11, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Kentucky Ranks Ahead of Key Early Opponents Going by Rothstein's metrics alone, Kentucky would be favored to open the season at 12-1 prior to SEC competition; call that a favorable schedule, an improved roster, or both. Whichever way you spin it, that'd more than do after last season's 9-4 non-conference finish.
Even at that rate, if Kentucky were to repeat their letdown 10-8 SEC finish, we'd still likely see these Wildcats land a few seeds higher in the postseason and, given they stay healthy, make a bigger splash than the just-departed team made in March.
But in my opinion, Pope is still one solid piece from making the competitive difference that would fully seperate this roster from the last one; it's a matter of great vs. national competitor. On that front, I've got two options.
Two Options for Kentucky's Final Addition The undeniably simpler move would be for five-star 2027 forward Ryan Hampton to reclassify and join the current team. With Kam Williams set to miss time, Hampton would be able to relieve his position on the wing and then some. He's a special prospect and shot-creator that would instantly raise the Cats' ceiling.
But Hampton has also expressed his desire to remain in the 2027 class, which is where Cade Tyson enters the picture.
Tyson would have to win his ongoing case for another year of eligibility, due to the NCAA's 5-in-5 rule, but the 6-foot-7 wing averaged nearly 20 points per contest (on a 41% clip from range) with Minnesota last season. Plug him in next to Milan Momcilovic, and you've got exactly the sort of dynamic duo that gives a team a permanent edge.
Are either of those likely? I'm not sure, but at this point, I wouldn't rule anything out in the NIL era of college hoops. I was almost surprised LeBron didn't announce he was committing to Ohio State for his final year of basketball, honestly.
